name: MUSE Cell Research Program (Tohoku University / Life Science Institute)
overview: Prof. Mari Dezawa's MUSE (Multi-lineage differentiating Stress Enduring) cells are a naturally occurring pluripotent stem cell population found in bone marrow, adipose tissue, and connective tissue. They are non-tumorigenic and home to sites of injury without external direction. The commercialized form (CL2020) is licensed by Life Science Institute (Mitsubishi Chemical). Active trials exist for ALS, stroke, and spinal cord injury; autism-specific clinical data is not yet published.

BioXcellerator states patients receive a Certificate of Analysis with each treatment. ISO 9001 certification claimed for laboratory processes. Independent third-party audit of Regencell's GMP status not publicly documented — request the current INVIMA authorization letter and cell CoA before proceeding.

name: Regenamex
overview: Regenamex is a regenerative medicine clinic founded in 2016 with primary operations in Puerto Vallarta and a second location in Tijuana, Mexico. They use allogeneic Wharton's Jelly MSCs and placental MSCs supplied by CBCells Biotechnology, which claims COFEPRIS (Mexico's federal health regulator) authorization and GMP manufacturing. The clinic is notable for celebrity endorser Ronnie Coleman — 8-time Mr. Olympia winner — who publicly promotes receiving infusions every four months. The autism protocol is individualized; no standard session count or dosing protocol is published. No peer-reviewed publications or clinical trial registrations exist for Regenamex's autism outcomes. All benefit claims are anecdotal. The clinic explicitly states stem cell therapy 'doesn't eliminate autism' but reports parent-observed improvements in attention, vocabulary, eye contact, and behavior at 3–6 months post-treatment.

The stems were shown to us microscopically so I know they are going to be effective! Very professional team.

However, CBCells' own website is inaccessible (401 error), no ISO certificate number or independent GMP audit is published, and no formal Certificate of Analysis is documented for patient distribution. One reviewer noted cells were shown microscopically at the clinic. COFEPRIS authorization is clinic-claimed but cannot be independently verified at this time.

museCellClaim.notes: Regenamex actively markets MUSE cells, featuring bodybuilder Ronnie Coleman as an endorser. No license from Tohoku University, Life Science Institute, or MuseCell Innovations (MCI) has been found. Regenamex is not listed in any MCI authorized provider registry, and their supplier CBCells Biotechnology is not identified as an MCI-authorized manufacturer. This follows the pattern MCI warns against: isolating SSEA-3+ subpopulations from MSC preparations and labeling them MUSE cells without authorization or verified characterization.

procedure.method: IV infusion (with intrathecal delivery available for some protocols) of umbilical cord and placental MSCs, plus exosomes and MUSE cells.
procedure.durationNotes: Not publicly specified — 1–3 sessions are published but total treatment duration in days is not; protocol is individualized per patient.

name: Linden Clinics
overview: Linden Clinics (also marketed as Linden Health and 'Linden Stem Cell') is an Istanbul, Turkey-based medical tourism clinic specializing in autism stem cell therapy. Marketing materials cite inconsistent experience figures — 'over 12 years' on one page and '18+ years' on another — and claim 2,000+ families treated from 40-45+ countries with a self-reported '94% success rate,' though no methodology or outcome scale backs that figure. The clinic describes using mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) sourced from umbilical cord tissue, bone marrow, or adipose tissue, without specifying which source is used for its autism protocol specifically. No lab partner, cell manufacturer, or GMP/ISO certificate number is disclosed; the clinic instead points to Turkey's International Health Tourism Authorisation Certificate, a facility/travel license rather than a cell-manufacturing quality standard. No peer-reviewed publications or registered clinical trials exist for its autism outcomes — all effectiveness claims are anecdotal, drawn from the clinic's own published success stories and third-party reviews. Pricing is not published; quotes are given only after a free consultation. Istanbul's medical tourism infrastructure and Linden's dedicated autism focus make it a frequently searched option for European and Middle Eastern families, though the lack of transparency around sourcing, certification, and pricing warrants added diligence.

location.address: Teşvikiye, Hakkı Yeten Cd. No:13, 34365 Şişli/İstanbul, Türkiye

fmtNotes: Linden Clinics has a blog article, "Therapies in Autism: From Stem Cells to Microbiome Research," discussing gut microbiota research in autism generally and mentioning "probiotic support" and "microbiome-focused strategies" — but it does not name FMT/fecal microbiota transplant specifically as a clinic-administered procedure, and no site-restricted search for FMT terms returned any indexed results. Not counted as a confirmed FMT offering.

communication.notes: Clinic's published success stories cite cases of first words and emerging sentences at 3-12 months post-treatment; no standardized outcome scale (e.g. CARS, ATEC) published

behavior.notes: Clinic reports general gains in 'attention span, sociability and autonomy'; no quantified behavior scale data published

featured.text: Our son was non-verbal after seven years of waiting for something to help. Months after his treatment at Linden he spoke his first words, and now repeats everything he hears — he's started counting and reciting the alphabet, and responds after one or two calls of his name instead of five.
For the first time in his life, our son said 'Mama' — a moment our family will never forget. His eye contact and engagement with us have also improved noticeably since the treatment.

cost.notes: Linden Clinics does not publish pricing for its autism program; quotes are provided only after a free consultation. Range estimated from comparable Istanbul autism stem cell programs — request an itemized quote and confirm what it covers before committing.

No lab partner name, ISO certificate number, GMP audit, or cell bank is disclosed anywhere on the clinic's site, and no patient-facing Certificate of Analysis (viability, sterility, lot number, donor screening) is described. Marketing pages also give inconsistent years-of-experience claims (12 vs. 18 years), a minor but notable transparency flag. Request the clinic's specific lab/cell-source documentation before proceeding.

name: Regeneration Clinic (ABC Protocol)
overview: Regeneration Clinic of Panama (also called Regenerate Panama), based in the Sortis Business Tower in Panama City, offers Wharton's Jelly umbilical cord MSC infusions in-house. For autism specifically, they co-market a three-stage "ABC Protocol" with two outside partners under a joint microsite (theabcofautism.com): Stage A is microbiome restoration via a partner called "Aflora," including FMT (fecal microbiota transplant), described as intended to prepare the gut to be receptive to the stem cell stage; Stage B is MeRT/neurofeedback via a partner called "BTC"; Stage C is the IV Wharton's Jelly MSC infusion, performed at Regeneration Clinic itself. This is a real, operating clinic with a named medical director and physical address, but the combined FMT+SCT program is a loosely coordinated multi-vendor marketing package rather than a single in-house, clinically documented protocol — no FMT delivery method, session counts, independent outcome data, or lab certification were found publicly.

location.address: Sortis Business Tower, Suite 4 (address also cited as Suite 4-i and "Oficina 13F, Calle 57 Este, Obarrio" on different pages — exact suite is inconsistent across the clinic's own site), Panamá

fmtNotes: FMT (Stage A of the "ABC Protocol") is not performed in-house by Regeneration Clinic — it's outsourced to a third party, "Aflora," bundled with a second third party ("BTC," MeRT/neurofeedback) under a joint marketing microsite (theabcofautism.com) separate from the clinic's own domain (regeneratepanama.com). Only the IV stem cell infusion (Stage C) happens at Regeneration Clinic itself. No FMT delivery method, session count, independent clinical evidence, or lab certification for the FMT component could be found. Aflora is described on-site as "a pioneer in FMT... in the world in children with ASD." Treat this as a coordinated package sold under joint branding, not a single clinic's integrated protocol.

communication.notes: No sample size, clinical trial, or clinic-specific outcome data found for the ABC Protocol or its autism patients

cost.notes: General clinic price range ($10,000–$30,000) covering airport transportation, bloodwork, IVs, and stem cell infusions for a 3–7 day stay — NOT confirmed as specific to the combined FMT+MeRT+stem cell autism package, which the site separately describes as spanning roughly 5 weeks of on-site treatment (an inconsistency between pages). Accommodation via partner Sortis Hotel, booked separately.

Do not confuse with the separate Panama City clinic "Stem Cell Institute" (cellmedicine.com), which does hold ISO 9001/GMP certification — that credential belongs to a different clinic and should not be attributed here.

procedure.method: IV infusion of Wharton's Jelly umbilical cord MSCs, performed at Regeneration Clinic itself. FMT (Stage A, via partner "Aflora") and MeRT/neurofeedback (Stage B, via partner "BTC") are delivered separately as part of the bundled "ABC Protocol" — no FMT delivery method is disclosed.
procedure.durationNotes: 3–7 days is the clinic's general stated range for the stem-cell-only portion (1–5 infusions). The joint "ABC Protocol" microsite separately describes the full combined program (with FMT + MeRT) as spanning roughly 5 weeks — a discrepancy between the clinic's own pages that isn't resolved publicly.

name: Chaitanya Stem-Cell Centre
overview: Chaitanya Stem-Cell Centre (part of Universal Hospital) in Pune, India offers both an autism stem cell protocol (umbilical cord MSCs and bone marrow cells; delivery route and cell sourcing model not clearly specified) and a separately listed FMT (fecal microbiota transplant) page nested under their autism-treatment site navigation. The two are not described anywhere as one combined bundled protocol — they read as cross-marketed separate service lines aimed at the same autism patient audience. Their FMT page cites "80%+ resolve" and "84% improvement in core ASD symptoms" statistics that loosely echo but misattribute/distort the real (unaffiliated) Kang et al. Microbiota Transfer Therapy studies (n=18 children, GI-symptom-focused), without naming any study, author, or citation. IMPORTANT: as of March 2026, India's National Medical Commission declared stem cell therapy illegal for autism (restricted to 32 approved conditions following a Feb 2026 Supreme Court ruling) — this clinic's live marketing of autism stem cell therapy appears to be in tension with that ruling.

location.address: CTS 1420, near Shaniwarwada, Kasba Peth, Pune 411037 (the clinic's own contact page and other listings inconsistently give the pincode as 411011)

fmtNotes: FMT is offered as a separate page/service (four delivery methods named: colonoscopy, enema, capsules, nasogastric tube; no session count or autism-specific delivery route specified) nested under the site's Autism Treatment navigation, cross-marketed to autism patients but not documented as bundled into one bought-together protocol with the stem cell service. The "80%+ resolve" and "84% improvement in core ASD symptoms" claims are not attributed to any named study — they loosely echo Kang et al. 2017/2019 Microbiota Transfer Therapy research (n=18, GI-symptom-focused, unaffiliated with this clinic) but the numbers don't cleanly match the published figures. Treat as unsourced marketing claims.

Autism is not on that list; the advisory explicitly called out private clinics in metropolitan and tier-2 cities marketing unproven stem cell treatments for autism and cerebral palsy. This clinic (Pune, a tier-2 city) was still actively marketing autism stem cell therapy on its live site as of this review (July 2026) — verify current legal status directly before proceeding.

name: Vinmec International Hospital — Stem Cell and Gene Technology Institute
overview: Vinmec Times City International Hospital in Hanoi (part of the JCI-accredited Vinmec Healthcare System) runs Vietnam's first government-approved clinical research program using autologous bone marrow mononuclear cells for autism spectrum disorder. An initial open-label trial (30 children, 2017-2019) was published in Stem Cells Translational Medicine in 2020, and a follow-up randomized, open-label, controlled Phase II trial (54 children, Dec 2021-Dec 2023) was published in Stem Cell Research & Therapy in 2025 — among the only peer-reviewed randomized trials of stem cell therapy for autism worldwide. Cells are processed at Vinmec's own accredited Stem Cell and Gene Technology Institute.

name: Biostar Angel Stem Cell Therapy (Osaka Trinity Clinic)
overview: In August 2025, Japan's Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) approved Biostar Stem Cell Technology Research Institute's autologous adipose-derived 'Angel Stem Cell' therapy for autism spectrum disorder under Japan's Act on Safety of Regenerative Medicine — the first ASD-specific stem cell therapy formally approved for clinical provision in Japan. Biostar is jointly operated by Korean firms R Bio and Nature Cell in partnership with Japan Angel Stem Cell (JASC); treatment is delivered at Osaka Trinity Clinic. Approval followed preclinical work showing improvement of core ASD-like symptoms in valproic-acid-induced autism mouse models; as of data verification, no peer-reviewed human autism efficacy publication has followed the approval.

name: Cellthera Clinic
overview: Cellthera Clinic, founded by Prof. MUDr. Jaroslav Michálek, has operated a regenerative-medicine facility in Brno, Czech Republic, since 2013, using a proprietary method for isolating stem cells from adipose and connective tissue. It holds a GMP Certificate for cell and tissue processing issued by the State Institute for Drug Control (SÚKL), the Czech national drug regulator, and reports having treated nearly 3,000 patients. The clinic's own listed specialties are orthopedics, neurology, cardiology, oncology, and plastic surgery; third-party medical-tourism aggregators list it among Czech providers of autism stem cell therapy, but Cellthera's own materials found during research did not explicitly confirm a dedicated autism protocol — treat the autism-specific claim as unconfirmed pending direct clinic verification.

name: Beijing Puhua International Hospital

Cell processing is regulated under China's National Health Commission (NHC) and National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) framework, which mandates GMP-certified cleanroom standards for cell-therapy manufacturing; no independent third-party audit of Puhua's specific facility was found during research, and the hospital's own case studies (not peer-reviewed publications) are the main public evidence of autism outcomes.
